subject: Re: Next steps — Enterprisecorp stakeholder map & procurement path
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jared Mills <jared.mills@enterprisecorp.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Next steps — stakeholder map & procurement path

Thanks again for the meeting this morning, Jared — great to meet the team and walk through Enterprisecorp's primary inference use cases. Quick recap and next steps from our side:

- Key decision criteria you called out: predictable latency under 150ms p95, unit cost below $0.002/token for high-volume batch requests, and enterprise-grade audit/logging for compliance.
- Stakeholders: you (product sponsor), Anna Lopez (legal), Procurement (procurement@enterprisecorp.com), and Mike Chen (platform engineering). Please correct if I missed anyone.
- Immediate asks from Enterprisecorp: procurement checklist + security questionnaire, and clarity on economic buyer and procurement timelines.

Proposed next steps:
1) Please share procurement/security contact and any checklist you prefer we fill out.
2) If procurement requires contract redlines up front, note the primary items (discount bands, SLAs, data residency).
3) We'll prepare a concise mutual action plan and route any buying-process exception requests internally for approvals.

I'll follow up separately with our internal approvals request (discount/SLA exceptions) once we have the checklist.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
(415) 555-0142

Thanks, Marissa — this matches our notes. A couple clarifications:

- Economic buyer: CFO (Elena Park) signed off on the budget category but final procurement review happens in ~3 weeks.
- Procurement runbook: please complete the attached checklist and return. Procurement will then kick off a standard review; expect legal redlines on indemnity and data retention.
- On discounts: procurement typically requires justification for anything >15% off list. If you expect to request >15%, please flag it for internal approvals.

I've attached our Procurement_Checklist (PDF).

Best,
Jared
Director of Product Management | Enterprisecorp

Forwarding Jared's checklist — Enterprisecorp has signaled they may expect >15% discount justification and will have legal/procurement review (Anna Lopez / procurement@enterprisecorp.com).

Why I'm looping you: procurement will likely want either a discount justification or a buying-process exception. They also will request SLA language changes (data retention & audit log wording). For this opportunity:
- ARR profile: $1.2M first-year run-rate, 3-year committed plan expected (quote to be finalized).
- Ask: approval for a buying-process exception up to 20% discount and approval for a limited SLA adjustment (availability target 99.9% with premium support and credits capped at 10% of monthly invoice).

Attachments: Enterprisecorp_Procurement_Checklist.pdf

Requested: can I get a quick thumbs on whether we can approve the exception and any constraints (finance/CSM/technical)? Need response today to keep procurement timeline this week.

Thanks,
Marissa

Marissa — thanks for the context and the ARR detail. Approvals below: 

- Discount: approve up to 20% one-time/first-year discount tied to a 3-year committed deal; must include a minimum annual commitment of $400k/year and a clause for quarterly business reviews.
- SLA: approve the temporary SLA exception to 99.9% availability for this customer, provided support is upgraded to our Premium+ plan and credits are capped at 10% of a monthly invoice. Legal to review final wording — loop in legal for signoff on indemnity/data retention adjustments.

Please include these constraints in the response to procurement and route any legal redlines to me + Stephanie. Tag the deal as DEAL-9876 in HubSpot and include the procurement checklist return.

Aditya Rao

- SLA: temporary exception to 99.9% availability if Enterprisecorp upgrades to Premium+ support; credits capped at 10% of monthly invoice.

3) If legal has immediate redlines, please share them and tag Aditya/Stephanie so we can expedite internal review.
